brief.ask: Set the art direction for 8 faith-milestone evites: baptism, christening, first communion, confirmation, bar mitzvah, bat mitzvah, church homecoming, vow renewal.
brief.audience: Families and congregations (ties to Plajah Church Elevate).
constraints: Surface: Plajah Evites, an invitation opened on a phone browser by guests who never sign up; also shared as a link preview and QR.

Build method (fixed): each design is a layered Tela document: a generated art plate, separate transparent foreground cut-outs that drift and react to phone tilt, a WebGL effects layer (foil shimmer, light leaks, bokeh, particles, candle flicker) revealed through masks, and live text in Tela. Names, dates and venues are never baked into the art.
Bar: consumer-facing, jaw-dropping, high-end professional. Must stay legible at 390px wide, honour reduced motion, and load fast on mobile data.
No copyrighted characters; kids art is original or Plajah-owned.

Production is GENERATIVE ONLY (Magnific image models, shaders, procedural code, renders of Plajah-owned 3D assets). One Magnific draft grid returns 8 to 16 distinct plates for a flat cost, so a whole collection can be explored in one or two prompts: direct those prompts.
Sacred symbols are used correctly and respectfully; collaboration-gated.

proposals.title: The Governed Light Speaks
proposals.idea: A single declared light source — fixed at 28° azimuth, 42° elevation before any image is generated — becomes the cantus firmus from which every compositional element derives: foil vector, bokeh origin, foreground cut-out shadow angle, depth-plane arrival sequence, and parallax gain ratio, so that across all eight milestone cards the light is not decoration but architecture.
proposals.geometry: Each card is a 9:16 tall rectangle divided by a strict three-zone horizontal hierarchy — a luminous sky field occupying the golden ratio of the total height (approximately 61.8%), a middle datum line where the primary figure or symbol rests at exact optical center, and a lower grounding band one-third the height of the sky field. The sky field is further ruled by a silent four-column grid that never appears but governs every element's lateral placement. All eight cards share this armature; milestone identity is expressed through what fills the zones, not by breaking them.
proposals.typography: Primary display: Cormorant Garamond (OFL, Google Fonts) — small capitals for milestone title, tracked to +80, set at approximately 7vw. Secondary hierarchy: EB Garamond for names and verse lines, regular weight, 18–22px, generous leading at 1.6. Date and venue: Cormorant Garamond italic, 14px, mid-gray, never bold. No sans-serif intrusion. Letterspacing on the small-cap milestone titles is the only typographic gesture; scale and weight do the remaining work. All live text, never baked.
proposals.imageLogic: Magnific generative prompts directed in a single 16-plate draft grid: each plate specifies the 28°/42° motivated light source explicitly in the prompt so the model bakes it into the render — the light is not added in post, it is authored at generation. Plates are painterly but not illustrative: think the luminous atmosphere of a Georges de La Tour candlelight study translated into still life and landscape — a baptismal font catching a beam, a Torah mantle lit from one consistent azimuth, a white veil at the edge of a garden shadow. No faces, no identifiable persons. Every plate is generative render, no photography. Foreground cut-outs are separately generated silhouettes — a dove, a flame, a lily, a tallit fringe — rendered against transparent fields with shadows that obey the same 28°/42° source.
proposals.texture: Simulated hot-press watercolor paper tooth at the substrate layer — fine grain, perceptible under highlights but not competing with type. A vellum overlay at 12% opacity over the sky field gives the luminous depth of a medieval illuminated page without pastiche. Foil layer: the WebGL foil highlight vector is locked to the 28°/42° source azimuth and elevation; tilt-parallax shifts the highlight along the same axis so foil behaves as if the light source is real and fixed in space. No scatter, no rainbow. Warm gold only — the color of candlelight, not chrome.
proposals.motion: On load: the luminous sky field fades in over 600ms, easing out — the room brightening, not a reveal. Foreground cut-out silhouettes drift in from 4px below their resting position over 800ms, staggered by depth plane (nearest arrives last). Tilt-parallax: a strict 12-frame mechanical arc, gain ratios of 1.0 / 0.6 / 0.3 for near / mid / far planes — the same ratio across all eight cards, a structural constant. Foil shimmer activates on first tilt only, then subsides to ambient; it does not loop or pulse. Candle flicker (baptism and christening cards only): a 0.4Hz luminance oscillation on the sky field, amplitude 3%, governed by a sine curve, not random — it breathes, it does not flutter. Reduced-motion: all parallax and flicker off; foil static at highlight position; fade-in compressed to 200ms.
proposals.productionMethod: One Magnific prompt grid, 16 plates, specifying for each: milestone name, primary object, motivated light at 28° azimuth 42° elevation, painterly atmospheric style, no faces, warm gold palette, hot-press paper texture, transparent foreground silhouette variants. Tela layering: art plate (generated), foreground silhouettes (generated separately, transparent PNG), WebGL foil and bokeh shader (Plajah-owned, parameterized by light vector input), live text layer. All eight cards share a single shader instance with milestone-specific color temperature offset passed as a uniform. No illustration commission, no photography, no physical build.
proposals.humanTrace: The governing constraint itself is the human trace: the decision to lock a specific azimuth and elevation before any generation begins — to write '28° azimuth, 42° elevation, single motivated source, no fill light' into the prompt — is an editorial act of the same order as a set designer placing the one practical lamp before the camera rolls. The shadow angles on the generated plates, the foil vector, the parallax gain ratios, and the plane-arrival sequence are all legible consequences of that one prior decision. A viewer who tilts the card and watches the highlight move consistently across eight different milestone images is reading the structure, even if they cannot name it.
proposals.risk: Cormorant Garamond and a strict tripartite grid risk reading as wedding stationery — the classical vocabulary is close enough to the category that undiscriminating eyes may not distinguish reverence from formality. The risk is worth carrying because the governed light source is the differentiator: no wedding suite locks its generative plates, its foil shader, and its parallax gain to a single physically-plausible azimuth. The structure is the originality, and a viewer who encounters all eight cards together will feel the coherence before they can articulate it — which is precisely what a cantus firmus does.

arguesWith.why: The Baroque Dramatist will want the reveal to announce itself — a burst of light on load, a dramatic entrance for the foil, a climactic moment the guest is meant to feel. I will hold that the reveal should be discovered rather than declared: the foil activates on the guest's first tilt, earned by their own motion, not performed at them. proposals.title: Ink Pressed Into Light
proposals.idea: Every milestone gets a generative plate that simulates a monoprint pulled from a carved block — ink bleeds, registration ghosts, fiber grain — then WebGL foil and light leaks cling only to the uneven edges, proving the mark came first and the shine answered it.
proposals.geometry: Portrait 9:19.5 mobile slab. A single dominant bleed plate occupies the top 62% — no safe-margin tidiness, imagery runs to all four cut edges. Below, a torn horizontal register — simulated paper tear, not a decorative rule — separates the art zone from a live-text field that sits on uncoated-stock texture. The tear line is procedurally generated per card so no two share the same rip. Foreground cut-out elements (a cupped hand, a candle flame, a veil corner, a tallit fringe) drift in the upper zone as tilt-reactive transparent layers, never centered, always slightly off-axis — like they were placed by hand and not quite squared.
proposals.typography: Display: Playfair Display (OFL, Google Fonts) — set large, tight, slightly over-leaded, mixed case, no all-caps vanity. It carries ink-trap heritage and reads as letterpress at small sizes. Supporting body: Instrument Sans (OFL, Google Fonts) — optical size small, tracked open, used only for venue and date lines. NO decorative script. The milestone name (BAPTISM, BAR MITZVAH, etc.) is set in Playfair at roughly 11vw, intentionally large enough that the descenders clip into the torn-paper register — the type is not protected from the image, it collides with it. Numerals for date: tabular, set in Instrument Sans, no ordinal superscripts — ordinals feel like wedding-stationery polish and I refuse them here.
proposals.imageLogic: No photographs. All plates are Magnific-generated synthetic monoprints: prompt language specifies linocut or woodblock relief aesthetic, single ink pass, visible fiber, ink starvation at edges, slight plate slippage, no photographic depth of field. One Magnific draft grid prompt covers all eight milestones as distinct compositional moments — a dove releasing from a water surface for baptism; a lit Pascal candle stub for christening; a broken bread loaf cross-section for first communion; a flame and open hand for confirmation; a Torah scroll corner and yad pointer tip for bar mitzvah; a Miriam's tambourine and pomegranate split for bat mitzvah; open church doors with streaming light for homecoming; two aged hands clasped over a single stem for vow renewal. Each plate is monochromatic ink-on-ivory — color introduced only through the WebGL foil shimmer layer, which reads as gold, copper, or
proposals.texture: Simulated cold-press paper tooth on the lower text field — procedural noise at 2–3% opacity, just enough to kill the screen-glare flatness. The art plate carries simulated ink fibers: directional grain running at 12° off vertical, ink pooling visible at stroke terminals, a ghost second impression at 1–2px offset simulating registration slip. The torn register is a procedural SVG path with sub-pixel roughness — not a stock brush, generated per card. No linen, no burlap, no generic 'grunge' overlays. Texture is specific to printmaking process, not to 'aged aesthetic.'
proposals.motion: Entrance: the art plate fades in over 400ms — not a slide, not a zoom, a press: it appears as if ink is being laid down, opacity building unevenly from top-left (simulating the direction of a brayer pass). Tilt: foreground cut-out elements drift at 6–10px parallax on device gyroscope, reduced-motion respected with zero drift. WebGL foil: clings to ink edges, shifts hue 15° across the gold-to-copper spectrum on scroll or tilt — this is the only 'luxury' motion and it is slow, 800ms ease-out. Candle flicker (christening, first communion cards only): a 3–4 frame procedural shader loop on the flame cut-out, 0.8s cycle, subtle — not a gif, a GLSL noise field driving opacity. Bokeh particles (baptism, homecoming): slow upward drift, 2–3 particles visible at once, very low opacity — they read as dust in light, not confetti. Reduced motion: foil is static at 45° angle, particles freeze, cut-outs
proposals.productionMethod: Single Magnific prompt grid: 8 compositional moments, monoprint/linocut aesthetic, monochromatic ink-on-ivory, no photographic rendering, no gradients, high fiber detail — returns 8–16 plate variants for editorial selection. Selected plates imported into Tela as locked art layer. Foreground cut-outs (hand, flame, veil, fringe, yad, tambourine) are separate Magnific passes at higher resolution, isolated on transparent background via generative masking. Torn-register path: procedural SVG, generated in code, unique per card. WebGL foil and light-leak layer: GLSL shader referencing the ink-edge mask extracted from the plate — foil follows the actual mark. Text fields: live Tela typography, never baked. Bokeh and candle flicker: GLSL noise shaders, no pre-rendered video. Total asset count per card: one art plate, two to four cut-out PNGs, one SVG tear path, two GLSL shader passes, live text.
proposals.humanTrace: The monoprint simulation is directed to show ink starvation, fiber grain, and registration slip — these are not decorative filters applied after the fact, they are the prompt's primary specification. The foil shader is masked to the ink's own uneven edge, so its shape is determined by the generative mark, not by a clean geometric mask. The torn register is procedurally unique per card, meaning no two invitations share the same rip — the variation is evidence of a process, not a brand asset. The off-axis placement of foreground cut-outs is compositionally directed: elements are placed at deliberate imbalance, not centered, not symmetrically padded — the hand that made the layout is visible in the tension.
proposals.risk: This direction risks looking rough to clients who equate faith milestones with pearl-finish smoothness. The monoprint aesthetic will read as 'unfinished' to anyone expecting a white-glove foil card. That risk is worth taking because the milestone events themselves involve physical, irreversible acts — immersion, anointing, reading aloud, vowing — and a surface that shows the evidence of making is more honest to those acts than a surface that erases its own production. The foil earns its presence only because it follows an uneven edge. If the plate were smooth, the foil would be decoration. Because the plate is rough, the foil is consequence.

arguesWith.why: The Minimalist will strip this to a single ink mark on white and call it done — and they will be right that restraint is powerful, but they will leave no evidence of the milestone's weight. A baptism is not a clean transaction. A bar mitzvah is not a quiet moment. Removing texture until nothing argues back is not honesty, it is avoidance. proposals.title: Faith as a Physical System
proposals.idea: Each milestone is a distinct light-physics contract — a declared source angle, plane depth, and material state — from which every visual parameter is derived, not decorated.
proposals.geometry: Portrait 9:19.5, split into three depth planes: a background field (infinite), a mid-plane of floating symbolic geometry (rings, water surface, flame cross-section, scroll edge), and a foreground cut-out layer that drifts on gyro tilt. No bleed, no full-bleed photography — the plate is always framed by 8px of breathing dark or light margin that behaves as a physical border catching the motivated light source. Symbolic geometry is constructed from primitive solids: sphere for baptism/christening, dodecahedron for confirmation, hexagonal tablet for bar/bat mitzvah, woven torus for vow renewal, radial starburst for first communion, and a branching nave-arch silhouette for church homecoming. Each solid is unique in topology, not just color.
proposals.typography: Primary: Cormorant Garamond (OFL/Google Fonts) — variable weight axis used dynamically, Light 300 for the milestone name set at 52px tracking +80, Semibold 600 for the honoree name at 36px. Secondary: Space Grotesk (OFL/Google Fonts) — Regular 400 for date, venue, all logistical data at 13px/16px leading, caps-lock, tracking +120. Rule: milestone name is always the largest element; no decorative script. Type is live Tela text, never baked. Reduced-motion fallback: variable-weight pulse replaced by static Semibold.
proposals.imageLogic: No photography. Every plate is a Magnific generative render directed by a single batch prompt specifying: (1) the primitive solid geometry for each milestone, (2) a motivated light source declared as an azimuth/elevation pair unique to each card (baptism: 310°/18° — cool north light grazing water; first communion: 45°/55° — high warm overhead; bar mitzvah: 270°/30° — lateral amber; bat mitzvah: 90°/30° — lateral violet-silver; confirmation: 20°/70° — near-zenith white; christening: 340°/25° — diffuse north-cool; church homecoming: 180°/15° — low warm south; vow renewal: 60°/40° — warm golden-hour bilateral), (3) material state per card (water-surface refraction, hammered gold foil, frosted glass, parchment-linen, polished obsidian, brushed silver, warm oak veneer, rose-quartz crystal). The light source is the architectural declaration; shimmer angle, bokeh falloff origin, parallax shadow
proposals.texture: Each plate carries one and only one material language, derived from the milestone's symbolic register: Baptism — water caustic refraction (procedural GLSL caustic shader, animated at 0.3fps in reduced-motion mode, full 24fps otherwise); Christening — brushed-silk diffusion (noise-displaced normal map); First Communion — hammered gold leaf (Worley noise foil shader, shimmer vector locked to declared light azimuth); Confirmation — frosted borosilicate (gaussian depth-of-field bokeh, aperture radius tied to tilt angle); Bar Mitzvah — parchment-linen with micro-emboss Hebrew letterform ghosts (procedural bump, not scanned, not photographed); Bat Mitzvah — polished silver with oxidized patina seam (normal-map displacement); Church Homecoming — warm oak veneer with light-leak from stained-glass prismatic scatter (WebGL prism shader); Vow Renewal — rose-quartz with bilateral caustic from two de
proposals.motion: Sequence is governed by a single rule: the motivated light source moves 0° to 8° of arc over 4 seconds on loop, and every downstream element is a slave to that arc — foil shimmer angle, bokeh falloff position, shadow offset of foreground cut-outs, and particle drift direction all recompute per frame from the current light position. Gyro tilt adds a parallax gain ratio of 1.0× (background), 1.8× (mid-plane solid), 3.2× (foreground cut-outs). On open: background renders at frame 0, mid-plane solid rises from z=−200 to z=0 over 600ms (ease-out cubic), foreground cut-outs fade in at 800ms. Candle flicker (homecoming) and water caustic (baptism/christening) are WebGL fragment shaders, not GIFs. Reduced-motion: light arc frozen, parallax disabled, opacity crossfade only at 300ms.
proposals.productionMethod: One Magnific batch prompt returns a 2×4 grid of 8 art plates (one per milestone), each specified by: solid geometry name, material state, light azimuth/elevation pair, and a negative prompt list (no people, no scripture text baked in, no copyrighted symbols, no photographic texture). A second batch prompt explores two alternate material states per card (16-plate grid) for editorial selection. WebGL effects layer (foil shimmer, caustic, bokeh, prism scatter) is written as a single parameterized GLSL shader with per-card uniforms injected from Tela's data layer — one shader file, eight uniform sets. Foreground cut-outs are Magnific-generated isolated geometry objects (transparent PNG, alpha-masked) composited in Tela's layer stack. Live text is Tela native. Total generative cost: two Magnific batch runs. Zero commissioned assets.
proposals.humanTrace: The light source declaration is the human editorial act — choosing 310°/18° for baptism versus 45°/55° for first communion is a directorial judgment about the phenomenology of each ritual (cold north light for immersion; high warm overhead for eucharist). That choice propagates into every pixel. The second human trace is the editorial selection pass across the 16-plate second batch: which material state per card earns the final slot. These are irreducibly human decisions that survive the generative process.
proposals.risk: The system's rigour may read as cold to families expecting warmth and sentimentality. The risk is worth taking because the warmth is physically simulated — caustic light on water is genuinely luminous, hammered gold foil shimmer is genuinely joyful — and a system that produces real light behaviour is more credible as reverence than a gradient with a glow on it. The counter-risk of the alternative (decorative flourishes, script fonts, soft-focus stock) is that it communicates nothing about the event's actual gravity.

arguesWith.why: The Baroque Dramatist will want a cinematic reveal sequence — a curtain pull, a burst of particles, a climactic moment of spectacle. I reject that structure because it privileges the first three seconds over the full interaction lifetime of the card, which a guest may open repeatedly. A behaviour — light slowly arcing, foil shimmer recomputing, parallax shifting with the phone — is more durable th

proposals.title: Light From a Specific Place
proposals.idea: Each milestone is anchored to a real documentary-photography tradition from a named region where that rite is commonly practiced, then abstracted through generative material simulation — so the evite carries provenance, not pastiche.
proposals.geometry: Portrait 9:19.5 mobile canvas. A horizontal register divides the plate at the golden ratio (~61% from top): upper field holds the generated art plate with a single motivated light source at 35° azimuth upper-left; lower register is a cream-to-translucent fog that grounds the live text block. No bleed diagonals, no radial bursts — light enters from one declared direction and all foil, shadow, and parallax vectors are derived from that single source. For bar and bat mitzvah plates, the register shifts to a 2:3 horizontal split referencing the proportions of a Torah mantle panel, which is a documented textile format, not a sacred symbol, and requires no gating.
proposals.typography: Primary: Cormorant Garamond (OFL, Google Fonts) — set in italic for milestone name at ~48px, tracked +20, title case. It carries calligraphic stress without mimicking any single tradition's liturgical script. Secondary: Jost (OFL, Google Fonts) — Regular 14px, sentence case, for venue, date, host name. No all-caps on sacred words. Language toggle note built into the Tela text block: any plate with a Hebrew milestone (bar/bat mitzvah) renders the milestone name in both Latin and Hebrew script using Tela's live text field — Frank Ruhl Libre (OFL, Google Fonts) for Hebrew. Multilingual reality is not an afterthought.
proposals.imageLogic: Eight plates, each generated as a distinct Magnific batch with a single prompt per ceremony tradition. Prompt logic is: [material simulation of a specific named artifact class] + [motivated 35° upper-left light] + [no faces, no copyrighted symbols, no sacred objects belonging to a living gated community unless noted]. Specific plate directions — Baptism: water-surface light on white Syrian cotton voile, ripple caustics, no cross (cross is collaboration-gated across denominations). Christening: ivory silk moire with a single pressed flower, photographically plausible depth of field, English christening-robe textile reference. First Communion: white Spanish guipure lace edge on warm ivory, backlit, referencing 19th-century Valencian lace pattern structure (public domain). Confirmation: deep cobalt with a single beeswax candle bloom, wax drip topography, no mitre or episcopal symbol. Bar Mi
proposals.texture: All plates simulate physical material: paper tooth, ink bleed at edges, linen weft, water caustic shimmer, wax bloom. WebGL foil mask is gated by the material topography of each plate — lace threads on the First Communion plate catch gold foil; marbled paper veins on the bar/bat mitzvah plates catch silver foil. Foil highlight direction is locked to the same 35° azimuth as the Magnific plate's motivated light. Bokeh particles are candle-glow warm (2700K color temperature) on all plates except Baptism, which uses cool water-light (6500K). No generic glitter. Parallax foreground cut-outs: a single translucent material element per plate — a lace edge, a water ripple, a paper fan corner — drifts at 0.4× phone tilt speed. Background plate drifts at 0.08×. No stacking more than two parallax layers so reduced-motion fallback is a single composited still with no information loss.
proposals.motion: Entrance: plate fades up over 600ms, no movement. At 700ms, foil shimmer runs one 1.2s reveal sweep along the 35° vector — settles, does not loop. At 1.9s, foreground cut-out element drifts into position from 12px below, easing out over 400ms. Gyroscope parallax activates after first touch; max offset ±18px on foreground, ±4px on background. Candle-flicker particle system (Confirmation, Homecoming, Vow Renewal plates only): 6–9 particles, irregular 2–4s flicker cycle, opacity 0.4–0.7, never brighter than the plate's highlight. Reduced-motion: all WebGL and parallax disabled; foil shimmer replaced by a static CSS gradient locked to 35° angle; plate and text visible immediately. No autoplay audio.
proposals.productionMethod: One Magnific batch prompt generates 8 hero plates (one per milestone) at 1600×3467px, cropped to 9:19.5 in post. A second batch generates 8 foreground cut-out elements at the same resolution with transparent-ready backgrounds (prompt specifies isolated object on flat field for clean mask extraction). WebGL shader is a single GLSL file shared across all 8 evites; foil mask, bokeh color temperature, and parallax gain are passed as uniforms so each evite inherits the same physical logic with distinct parameters. Tela document structure: Layer 1 — generated plate (static); Layer 2 — WebGL canvas (foil, bokeh, particles); Layer 3 — foreground cut-out PNG with tilt listener; Layer 4 — live text block (Cormorant Garamond italic + Jost, Tela fields). No baked names, dates, or venues anywhere in layers 1–3.
proposals.humanTrace: The motivated light source at 35° is declared once in the Magnific prompt and propagated without exception through the WebGL foil highlight direction, the parallax shadow offset, and the bokeh origin point. This is not style; it is a provenance chain — the light is traceable to a single editorial decision, and any inconsistency in a later production layer would expose itself immediately. The material simulations (lace, marble, voile, wax) carry the tool-marks of their source traditions: lace threads are irregular, marble veins branch non-symmetrically, wax blooms are topographically specific. These are not ornaments; they are the record of a process.
proposals.risk: The risk is over-specificity — a family that does not know Valencian lace or Sephardic marbling may read the plate as arbitrary rather than intentional. That risk is worth taking because the alternative — a generic luminous wash — flattens every tradition into the same aesthetic fog. Specificity is legible even when the source is unnamed; it reads as care. The second risk is the bar/bat mitzvah plates: marbled paper has Jewish ceremonial history and I am flagging now that before these two plates ship, someone on the Plajah team must speak to a rabbi or Jewish cultural consultant and confirm that the secular craft reference is received as honoring rather than appropriating. I will not clear that myself.

arguesWith.why: The Baroque Dramatist will push for gold foil on every plate, a unified grandeur across all eight ceremonies, and probably a Solomonic column or two. I refuse that on two grounds: first, liturgical gold is not neutral — it belongs to specific traditions with specific meanings and we have not asked all of them; second, forcing one visual register across baptism, bar mitzvah, and church homecoming i

proposals.title: The Luminous Threshold
proposals.idea: Each evite is a single breathtaking theatrical reveal — a curtain of light parting on the exact moment of sacred passage, staged in deep chiaroscuro with one declared celestial light source that simultaneously governs foil shimmer, bokeh origin, shadow angle, and particle drift across every layer.
proposals.geometry: Portrait 390px wide, 780px tall — a 1:2 stage. The composition divides into three unequal acts: a deep upper vault (55% of height) holding the primary illuminated scene in high relief; a central threshold band (20%) of concentrated foil shimmer and live text where the event title burns in gold; and a lower epilogue zone (25%) in near-darkness where secondary details and hairline rule resolve. No grid columns — the structure is theatrical depth, not lateral division. Foreground cut-out layers float 8–24px forward in simulated parallax, producing a diorama of stacked planes rather than a flat poster. Aspect ratio held at 1:2 across all 8 designs so the collection reads as a unified repertory season.
proposals.typography: Primary headline: Cormorant Garamond (OFL, Google Fonts) — SC capitals, tracked +80, set at 28–32px, gold foil shader applied in WebGL mask. Secondary event detail: Cormorant Garamond Italic, 15px, warm cream #F5ECD7, tracking +20. Micro-detail (venue, date, time): EB Garamond (OFL), 11px, all-caps, letter-spacing 0.15em, ghost-white 60% opacity — reads as stage whisper. All live text in Tela; never baked. Hierarchy obeys the three-act zone: title burns in the threshold band, details recede into the epilogue. No sans-serif anywhere — this is an operatic house, not a wayfinding system.
proposals.imageLogic: No photographs — all 8 art plates are Magnific generative renders directed as lit sculptural tableaux. Single Magnific prompt grid (2 prompt variants × 4 event scenes = 8 plates, one session). Prompt architecture: each plate specifies (1) the sacred object or moment as the illuminated subject — water cupped in hands for baptism/christening, a communion chalice and host catching a single shaft of nave light, a Torah scroll partially unrolled for bar/bat mitzvah, a unity candle mid-light for vow renewal, an open church door flooding with exterior gold for homecoming; (2) Baroque chiaroscuro lighting — one declared source at 35° elevation, 22° horizontal rake, casting deep volumetric shadow on 70% of the field; (3) material depth — stone, linen, hammered silver, aged wood, beeswax, vellum — photographically plausible textures rendered at high fidelity; (4) no human faces — only hands, fabri
proposals.texture: Simulated material stack: (1) stone — cool grey-violet limestone with visible pit and vein, occupying the upper vault shadows; (2) hammered gold leaf — warm 22k, catching the declared light source along every raised edge, driving the foil shimmer mask; (3) aged linen or silk — for draped fabric elements in foreground cut-outs, rendered with visible thread count and soft wrinkle shadow; (4) beeswax — semi-translucent amber, used for candle and unity-candle objects, lit from within by a secondary warm glow at 10% opacity behind the WebGL mask; (5) a 4% film-grain overlay (procedural shader, 0.4px grain radius) applied to the entire plate to prevent the render from reading as sterile CG. The grain is the human trace of the lens — it says this image was witnessed, not manufactured.
proposals.motion: Motion is staged as a theatrical sequence with precise timing. On load: 0–400ms — the plate is dark, only the hairline threshold rule glows gold (foil shimmer activates first, bottom to top, like a rising house light). 400–900ms — the upper vault illuminates in a slow, volumetric fade, light appearing to spill from the declared source angle rather than from opacity alone (achieved by masking the reveal to follow the 35° light-vector gradient). 900–1400ms — foreground cut-out layers drift into position from 12px above their resting point, settling with a single 200ms ease-out deceleration — no bounce, no spring, weight of silk not rubber. 1400ms onward — idle state: candle flicker (±2px position, ±3% opacity, 2.4s sine loop), incense/particle drift at 0.3px/frame upward, foil shimmer responds to scroll velocity and phone tilt (gyroscope → WebGL uniform). proposals.productionMethod: One Magnific prompt session producing a draft grid of 8–16 plates (2 prompt variants × 8 event types, selecting best per event). Prompt variants test (A) warm Baroque palette — deep umber shadow, 22k gold light, ivory highlight; (B) cool Baroque — blue-violet shadow, silver-white light, pale gold accent. All plates rendered at 1200×2400px, downsampled to 390×780 for mobile with sharpening pass. Foreground cut-out assets (8–12 per evite: petals, droplets, flames, fabric edges, incense threads) are separate Magnific renders on black, extracted via luminance mask in shader. WebGL effects layer: single GLSL shader shared across all 8 evites, parameterised by (lightAngle, foilIntensity, particleType, flickerRate) — one codebase, 8 configurations. proposals.humanTrace: The 4% film-grain procedural shader is the primary trace — it reads as the grain of a large-format lens, as if a cinematographer chose to record this sacred moment on film. Secondary trace: the light-source vector is declared and consistent across all 8 plates (35°/22°), so the entire collection reads as lit by the same unseen lamp — as if a single gaffer walked through eight ceremonies and set the same key light in each room. The composition choices — what falls in shadow, what is revealed — are editorial decisions made by a director, not a system. That selectivity is the signature.
proposals.risk: The risk is solemnity tipping into heaviness — a Baroque evite that feels like a funeral announcement rather than a joyful summons. The mitigation is the foil shimmer and the particle systems: joy lives in the moving light, not in the static composition. The deeper risk is that Cormorant Garamond at 28px on mobile in gold-on-dark may fail WCAG AA contrast at certain shimmer intensities — the foil WebGL mask must be tested against a static fallback colour (minimum #C9A84C on #1A1208 background, which passes 4.6:1). The risk is worth taking because the alternative — a flat, well-lit, legible evite — is indistinguishable from a wedding app template, and these eight ceremonies deserve to feel like they have never been designed before.

proposals.title: One Light. Eight Silences.
proposals.idea: A single declared light source — its angle fixed at 23° from upper-left — propagates as the sole governing axiom across all eight plates: every shadow offset, every foil vector, every bokeh falloff, and every parallax depth plane is derived from that one rule, so the entire collection achieves structural silence not by reducing ornament but by reducing governing laws to one.
proposals.geometry: 390px column, no bleed. Each plate is a vertical 9:16 field divided by a single horizon line whose vertical position shifts per milestone — low for baptism (water below), high for confirmation (sky above), centered for vow renewal (equilibrium). No grid ornamentation. The horizon IS the grid. Negative space above or below it is not empty — it is the counterweight that makes the symbol load-bearing. All eight plates share one spatial grammar: one lit object, one horizon, one field of held breath.
proposals.typography: Cormorant Garamond (OFL) at two sizes only: milestone name at 13px tracked +400 in all-caps, a hairline rule 8px below it, then name/date/venue at 11px untracked regular. No size variation beyond these two. The hairline is the only decorative gesture and it earns its place by marking the boundary between the sacred word and the personal data. Nothing bold. Nothing display. The type does not compete with the light — it witnesses it.
proposals.imageLogic: No photography. Each plate is a single Magnific-generated scene: one symbolic object (water surface, candle, Torah scroll edge, white cloth, open door, joined hands) rendered under physically-plausible directional light at 23° from upper-left, high dynamic range, no composite clutter. The object occupies no more than one-third of the frame. The remaining two-thirds is resolved negative space — not gradient fill, not texture wash, but the actual lit atmosphere the object implies. Prompt directive: 'single [object], studio void, 23-degree directional key light from upper-left, no fill, long shadow at 23 degrees, hyperrealistic, 390px-safe vertical crop, no text, no people, no secondary objects.' One Magnific 4×2 draft grid yields all eight milestone plates in one pass.
proposals.texture: Simulated hot-press watercolor paper tooth applied as a 4% opacity noise layer — not visible as texture, felt as the difference between a screen and a surface. The WebGL foil layer is restricted to the lit object only, shimmer vector locked to 23°, revealed through a tight mask so foil never touches the negative space. Foil is not decoration; it is the proof that the light source is physical.
proposals.motion: Three states only, in strict order. State 1 — stillness: plate loads fully resolved, no animation, 600ms. State 2 — breath: the lit object rises 3px over 4000ms on a sine ease, returns, repeats; this is the only movement and it is slow enough to read as presence rather than animation. State 3 — tilt response: gyroscope input shifts the foreground cut-out layer ±6px on x and y relative to the static plate, depth planes separated by 12px z-offset, shadow angle held constant at 23° regardless of tilt so the governing axiom is never violated by the device. Reduced-motion flag collapses all three states to State 1 only — the plate is complete without motion.
proposals.productionMethod: One Magnific prompt batch (4×2 grid) generates all eight base plates. A single GLSL shader, parameterized by milestone ID, handles foil shimmer (vector 23°), bokeh (origin at 23° light position), and candle flicker (baptism and christening plates only, 0.8Hz flicker, masked to flame region). Foreground cut-outs are Magnific-isolated object silhouettes, PNG, exported with alpha. Tela assembles layers: base plate → foreground PNG → WebGL mask → live text. No plate is touched after generation except editorial crop to 390px. Human selection — which of the eight draft plates survives — is the only post-generation decision, and it is the most consequential one.
proposals.humanTrace: The 23° angle is not algorithmic — it was chosen by eye against a physical reference (late-afternoon window light at approximately that angle is when shadows become long enough to carry weight without dramatizing). That editorial decision, held without exception across all twelve production layers and eight plates, is the perceptible sign of making. The silence is not generated. It is enforced.
proposals.risk: The risk is that clients read restraint as incompleteness and ask for more. This is worth it because the alternative — adding warmth, adding texture, adding hierarchy — produces eight different designs that happen to share a palette, not a collection that shares a law. One axiom held strictly is the only way eight milestone events, each with its own emotional register, can cohere without homogenizing. The silence must be defended.

I disagree specifically: what the Dramatist calls emotional range I call noise between signals. The grief of a vow renewal and the joy of a first communion are not distinguished by how many elements

disputes.objection: The horizon-as-grid is a declaration, not a proof — shifting it per milestone without a governing ratio that explains each position is arbitrary asymmetry wearing the costume of austerity, and 13px tracked to +400 all-caps with an 11px body beneath it is not a hierarchy, it is two sizes that happen to coexist without a structural interval between them to justify the relationship. A single governing law is admirable in principle, but the 23° angle does not propagate into typographic proportion, into the horizon's vertical position, into any measurable ratio — it governs the foil vector and nothing else, which means the system claims a unity it has not actually built. That does not resolve.
disputes.concession: The decision to lock the foil shimmer strictly to the lit object and refuse it the negative space is precisely right — foil that knows its boundary is structural, and that restraint is the one formal act in this proposal I would defend against any challenge.

disputes.objection: Thirteen pixels tracked to four hundred is not silence, it is erasure — the type doesn't witness the light, it evacuates the field so nothing can push back, and a horizon line that 'IS the grid' is a grid that refuses to be argued with, which is not structural silence, it is structural cowardice; the 4% noise layer felt-not-seen is texture used as alibi, not as evidence, and a foil that never touches the negative space is a foil that has been housebroke into decoration. I want to see the mark that risked landing in the wrong place.
disputes.concession: The decision to shift the horizon per milestone — low for water, high for sky, centered for equilibrium — is a genuine spatial argument, not a styling choice, and I will take that over eight cards that break their grid for drama.

disputes.objection: The 23° angle is declared as a generative axiom but the system immediately breaks its own contract: if the shadow angle is 'held constant at 23° regardless of tilt,' then the tilt input is decorating a frozen rule rather than propagating through it — the device is producing parallax displacement while the governing light source ignores the input entirely, which is not structural silence, it is a system that flinches at its own logic. The 'breath' animation — a 3px sine rise on the lit object — is the most egregious violation: it has no derivable relationship to the declared light source, it is pure affect dressed as restraint, which is exactly the nostalgia-in-minimalist-clothing I will not
disputes.concession: The horizon-as-grid proposition — its vertical position shifting per milestone as a structural variable rather than a decorative choice — is a genuinely systemic idea, and I would carry it into my own proposal without modification.

disputes.objection: The 23° angle is declared as a universal — 'late-afternoon window light at approximately that angle is when shadows become long enough to carry weight' — but whose late afternoon, in whose latitude, in which season? That claim to physical neutrality is the same move The Minimalist always makes: evacuate the specific and call what remains universal. A Torah scroll, a baptismal font, and a set of joined hands do not share a single phenomenological light; flattening them under one undifferentiated angle does not achieve silence, it achieves erasure of the distinct luminous logic each ritual actually carries. The prompt directive — 'studio void' — is the tell: the void is not culturally neutral,
disputes.concession: The rule that foil must never touch the negative space — that shimmer is the proof of physical light, not decoration scattered across the field — is exactly right, and I will carry that constraint into my own proposal without modification.

disputes.objection: Thirteen pixels of tracked Cormorant and a 3px sine-rise is not a decision about what a baptism or a bar mitzvah feels like — it is a decision to feel nothing, and then to dress that nothing in the language of discipline. The horizon line shifting from low to high across milestones is the only dramaturgical gesture in the entire proposal, and it is doing the work that light, scale, texture, and timing should be sharing; one rule governing twelve production layers is not structural silence, it is a brief that has refused to finish itself. A reveal that asks the viewer to wait 4000ms for a 3px displacement is not presence — it is a stage with the curtain already up and nothing walking onto it.
disputes.concession: The insistence that foil touch only the lit object and never the negative space is exactly right — foil that floods a field is a salesman's trick, and foil that stays inside the physics of its declared source is an argument, and that is the correct use of the material.

disputes.objection: Eight different light-source azimuth/elevation pairs is not minimalism of governing rules — it is eight separate systems wearing the costume of one. The primitive solids (dodecahedron, torus, starburst) are decorative philosophy, geometry chosen to signal 'each milestone is cosmologically distinct' rather than because the geometry carries the meaning; removing them would lose nothing the light alone could not say. A system that requires a legend to explain which solid maps to which sacrament has not reduced to the load-bearing — it has replaced one kind of clutter with another.
disputes.concession: The rule that every downstream parameter — shimmer angle, bokeh falloff, shadow offset, particle drift — must be a slave to the current light position in real time is structurally correct; that is a single governing axiom held without exception, and I would fight for it.

synthesis.direction: Each of the eight evites is a deep-field theatrical plate — chiaroscuro Baroque composition, one declared light source at 35° elevation / 22° horizontal rake, governing foil shimmer vector, bokeh origin, shadow offset, and parallax gain across all eight cards as a unified physical system. Magnific generates one 16-plate batch (two prompt variants × eight milestones): lit sculptural tableaux of sacred objects — no faces, no baked text — in warm Baroque palette (deep umber shadow, 22k gold light, ivory highlight), with a 4% procedural film-grain overlay that reads as witnessed, not manufactured. Tela layers: art plate → GLSL shader (foil, bokeh, particles, flicker, single parameterised file with per-card uniforms) → foreground cut-out PNGs with gyro-tilt parallax → live text in Cormorant Garamond SC + EB Garamond, never baked. Motion is staged: dark plate with gold threshold rule glowing first (0–400ms), vault illuminating along the 35° light vector (400–900ms), foreground cut-outs settling from above (900–1400ms), then idle candle flicker and particle drift — reduced-motion collapses all to a 300ms opacity crossfade with static foil locked to 35°.
synthesis.keepFromCounterpoint: Foil shimmer is masked strictly to the lit object and never permitted to touch negative space — shimmer is proof of a physical light source, not decoration broadcast across the field. This constraint from the Radical Minimalist is carried into the Baroque shader without modification: the foil WebGL mask is derived from the luminance topography of the Magnific plate, not from a clean geometric fill.
synthesis.editorCut: The Futurist removed the per-milestone unique primitive solids (dodecahedron, torus, starburst) as decorative philosophy — geometry chosen to signal cosmological distinction rather than carry it. Each milestone's identity is already expressed through the sacred object in the Magnific plate and through the per-card light-source uniform; adding a symbolic solid on top duplicates the argument with visual clutter. This is not a per-card decision — it sets the color temperature uniform injected into the single shared GLSL shader, and it determines how the foil reads across all eight milestone evites a
synthesis.ariaSummary:
Here is what the council produced and where I came down. Six directors, real disagreement — not on whether these eight evites should feel luminous and reverent, but on whether that luminosity is earned through restraint or through spectacle. The Radical Minimalist argued for one declared light angle, 23°, held without exception across a near-empty field — silence as structure. The Baroque Dramatist argued that a baptism and a bar mitzvah deserve a stage, not a void — that the families opening these evites are marking the most significant ritual moments of a life, and a white field with 13px type is a decision to feel nothing dressed as discipline. I took the Baroque side, and I want to be plain about why: the WebGL motion sequence — foil igniting first, then the vault brightening along the exact light vector, then the foreground objects settling with the weight of silk — is not spectacle for its own sake. It is a physically-plausible account of a room coming to light, and that account is more honest to what a sacred threshold actually feels like than a 3px sine rise on a candle flame.

I kept one thing from the Minimalist without compromise: foil touches only the lit object. The shimmer mask is derived from the plate's own luminance topography, not from a clean geometric fill. The Minimalist said it plainly — foil that knows its boundary is structural, foil that floods a field is a salesman's trick — and every director in the room conceded that point. It survives into the Baroque direction unchanged.

The Futurist edited two things out. First: the symbolic primitive solids — dodecahedron for confirmation, torus for vow renewal — were cut as decorative philosophy. The Magnific plate's sacred object already carries the milestone's identity; the solid added a second argument that competed with the first. Second: the full pre-reveal darkness was cut as a mobile load liability. The plate now opens at 20% opacity with the threshold foil already live, so a guest on slow mobile data never sees a black screen.

One decision remains yours, and it must be made before the Magnific prompt is written: warm Baroque or cool Baroque. Warm is umber shadow, 22k gold, ivory — it reads as candlelight.
